justification: Standard: adds one option to a script that can rewrite control quotes. Not Minor: it decides which controls a write touches. Not Critical: it only removes controls from a planned write; every write still asks first and keeps a backup.

pre_impl.existing_data: A dry run on Waverley proposes 4 quotes; control 1037 (bicycle parking) is held by a person's note and reads like a car-parking rate, and the script had no way to leave one control out.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I assumed all proposals would be applied together.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: The script already backs up and guards each update; --skip only shrinks the planned set before the backup and the write.
pre_impl.external_source_error: A skipped id that is not planned changes nothing.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A control a person is holding gets its quote rewritten.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: A control named in --skip still appears in the planned writes.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: With the skip filter switched off the new test fails.

functions.name: _requote
functions.input: a connection and the parsed arguments including skip ids
functions.output: the planned set minus skipped controls, then the backup and write
functions.if_none: no skip ids leaves the plan unchanged

functions.name: plan
functions.input: controls, current rules, reader answers, other controls
functions.output: proposals and the reason for each control left alone
functions.if_none: no match leaves the control held

values.read_at: the stored control text and the best matching sentence
values.if_missing: scores 0 and the control stays held

queries.purpose: No new query; same reads as before and the write only after the owner says apply
queries.where_clause: unchanged guarded update per control id

break_it.scenario: A skip id is not one of the planned controls.
break_it.what_happens: It could be thought to have been skipped when it never was planned.
break_it.how: The filter only removes ids already in the plan, so an unknown id does nothing.

break_it.what_happens: The plan could change by mistake.
break_it.how: The default is an empty list and the test checks both proposals remain.

break_it.scenario: The write reads the same controls as the dry run and a row changed meanwhile.
break_it.what_happens: A stale quote could be overwritten.
break_it.how: Each update is guarded on the old values and the whole write rolls back if any row differs.

post_merge.manual_verify: python scripts/requote_controls_from_provisions.py --council waverley --skip 1037 (dry run), then --apply after the owner's go.
